manager.findings: Gross performance of 4.72 basis points on $1,144.3995 in entry notional fell short of 10.62 basis points of round-trip commissions. There was no four-READY decision. The final 15-minute sample weakened win rate and mean net. Across the first 170 closes, 106 official 15-minute pairs moved from 26 to 22 winners and reduced mean net by $0.05159877. The 30-minute sample is still pending. The latest delayed basket justifies measuring pre-submit phases separately from the hold-duration decision.
manager.recommendation: Retain the ten-minute timer, three-contract exposure, IOC guards and frozen four-READY test. Prospectively measure observer wake and session startup, the account and history reads, each due check, pre-submit and acknowledgement, along with exchange creation and fill timestamps. Record monotonic phase durations, queue size and basket association. Compare per-basket due-to-send median, 95th percentile and fraction above ten seconds. Reproduce the observed phases offline before considering a scheduling change. For IOC research, distinguish missing depth, repeated books and guarded orders from partial or zero fills.

ceo.rationale: Keep current order size, timer and risk limits. The available paired evidence and two IOC probes support further measurement. Observe timer phases before changing execution and preserve the frozen later test for any performance change.
